subject: language_arts

unit.title: Apostrophes & homophones
unit.essentialQuestion: When does a word need an apostrophe, and how do I pick between sound-alike words?

title: Apostrophes job 2: belonging (possession)
objectives: By the end, I can use 's to show that something belongs to someone.

vocabulary.definition: belonging — when something is owned by someone
vocabulary.example: Sam's bag = the bag belongs to Sam

vocabulary.definition: the person or animal something belongs to
vocabulary.example: in 'the dog's bone', the dog is the owner

vocabulary.definition: the mark we add to the owner's name to show belonging

emphasize: The apostrophe's Job 2: add 's to the OWNER to show something belongs to them — the cat's tail = the tail of the cat.
The move: find who owns it → add 's to the owner (never to the thing owned).
Keep it concrete with belonging labels; hold the plural trap for Lesson 13 but note any cats'/plural confusion.

keyConcepts: the X of the Y ↔ the Y's X
misconceptions: putting 's on the thing instead of the owner (bag's Sam)
confusing possession with a plural s (noted here, tackled fully in Lesson 13)
hooks: A tiny 's turns a name into a label that TELLS you who owns something — let's label the room.

digital: phrase-flip animations (the X of the Y → the Y's X)

plan.goal: Show that a tiny 's makes a word TELL you who owns something; retrieve Job 1 as the contrast.
plan.note: The belonging-label frame carries the lesson. Quick retrieval: contract do not.
plan.successCriteria: Child answers don't for the retrieval and is curious about the second job.

script.say: Whose pencil is this? Watch — I can make a word TELL you who it belongs to. I just add a tiny apostrophe-s. Mia plus 's — Mia's pencil — the pencil belonging to Mia! Let's make belonging labels today. But first, quick memory check: yesterday the apostrophe had a squashing job. Contract do not for me.
script.adaptHints: Listen for don't. If shaky, re-show do not → don't quickly, then: 'today the apostrophe has a SECOND, totally different job.' Swap 'pencil' for an object the child actually owns.

blocks.caption: Mia's pencil — the label tells you who owns it!

stuckProtocol: If the retrieval stalls: write do not, cross the o, place the apostrophe together — one squash, then move on to the new job.

plan.goal: Model Job 2 on three phrases: find the owner, add 's — the cat's tail = the tail of the cat.
plan.note: Underline the owner each time BEFORE adding 's. The table makes the flip visible.
plan.successCriteria: Child can say the trick: find the owner, add 's right after their name.

script.say: Job two of the apostrophe: belonging. If something belongs to someone, I add apostrophe-s to the owner. Watch: the cat's tail — that means the tail of the cat. The 's on cat says 'this belongs to the cat'. Sam's bag — the bag belonging to Sam. The trick: find the OWNER, add 's right after their name. The dog owns the bone — so it's the dog's bone.
script.adaptHints: Underline the owner out loud each time: 'who owns it? … THAT word gets the 's.' Keep the rhythm: owner first, then 's.

blocks.caption: Find the owner → add 's to the owner.

plan.goal: Shared flips: the bone of the dog → the dog's bone; the desk of the tutor → the tutor's desk. Child finds the owner first every time.
plan.note: Child names the owner, then completes the flip in the fillBlank.
plan.successCriteria: Child names the owner correctly and completes the dog's bone flip.

script.say: Turn this around with me: the bone of the dog. Who's the owner? The dog! So it becomes… the dog's bone. Now you finish this one on screen. And then try me one more: the desk of the tutor — who's the owner, and how does it flip?
script.adaptHints: If the child grabs the wrong word, ask 'who OWNS it?' before anything else. Praise the owner-hunt, not just the answer.

blocks.text: the bone of the dog → the ___ bone

check.question: Flip it: the desk of the tutor.

wrongAnswers.why: belonging shown but the apostrophe forgotten
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does the desk belong to the tutor? Then the tutor needs the apostrophe-s to show it. Where does it go?

wrongAnswers.why: put 's on the thing, not the owner
wrongAnswers.remedy: Who OWNS the desk? The tutor. The 's goes on the owner — say 'the tutor's…' and finish it.

plan.goal: Diagnostic: show the bag belongs to Sam — apostrophe present AND on the owner.
plan.note: Options carry the two key errors: Sams (no apostrophe) and Sam bag's (on the wrong word).
plan.successCriteria: Child picks Sam's bag and can say why the 's sits on Sam.

script.say: Your turn alone. Write it to show the bag belongs to Sam. Think: who's the owner, and what does the owner get?
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'Where did the 's go, and why there?' — listen for 'on Sam, the owner'.

blocks.prompt: Which shows that the bag belongs to Sam?
blocks.explain: Sam is the owner, so Sam gets the apostrophe-s: Sam's bag.

check.question: Write it to show the bag belongs to Sam.

wrongAnswers.why: forgot the possessive mark
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does the bag belong to Sam? Then Sam needs 's to show it. Sam's bag.

wrongAnswers.why: put 's on the thing, not the owner
wrongAnswers.remedy: Who OWNS the bag? Sam. The 's goes on the owner — Sam's bag.

plan.goal: Independent belonging labels: flip 'the X of the Y' phrases and write labels for real things at home.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Always ask 'who's the owner?' before the child writes. Note (don't teach) any plural confusion for Lesson 13.
plan.successCriteria: Child writes 3+ possessive phrases with 's correctly on the owner.

script.say: Label-maker time! I'll give you long phrases — you flip each one into a belonging label. And every time, tell me first: who's the owner?
script.adaptHints: Use real people and pets from the learner's life for the labels (Mum's mug, Rex's bowl). Never move the 's off the owner.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'let's find the owner first.'
Step down: give the phrase with the owner underlined; child only adds 's.
ONE hint: 'ask: who does it belong to?'
Keep it safe: 'Belonging is all about the owner — let's find who owns it.'

plan.goal: Child states Job 2 and where the 's goes; end on a win.
plan.note: Child-led. Tease Lesson 13's trap without teaching it.
plan.successCriteria: Child says: 's shows belonging and goes on the owner.

script.say: Tell me the apostrophe's second job, and where the 's goes. … Yes — belonging, and the 's goes on the OWNER. You found the owner every time and gave them their 's — your belonging labels are spot on. Next time, a warning: some apostrophes out in the world are FAKES, and you're going to catch them.
script.adaptHints: Praise the observed process: hunting the owner before writing. The 'fake apostrophes' teaser sets up Lesson 13.

block.prompt: The pencil belongs to Mia. Which is right?
block.explain: Mia is the owner, so Mia gets the apostrophe-s: Mia's pencil.

wrongAnswers.why: no apostrophe — the belonging is unmarked
wrongAnswers.remedy: The pencil belongs to Mia, so Mia needs her little belonging mark. What goes between Mia and the s?

wrongAnswers.why: 's on the thing owned instead of the owner
wrongAnswers.remedy: Who owns the pencil? Mia! The 's always sits on the owner's name.

reteach.say: Belonging labels always start with the owner. Mia owns the pencil → Mia's pencil. Owner first, 's on the owner, then the thing.

practiceBank.skill: flip 'the X of the Y' into 'the Y's X'

block.text: the tail of the cat → the ___ tail

wrongAnswers.why: no apostrophe — looks like more than one cat
wrongAnswers.remedy: Without the apostrophe, cats means lots of cats! We want ONE cat who OWNS the tail. What does the owner get?

wrongAnswers.why: 's on the thing owned
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does the tail own the cat, or does the cat own the tail? The 's goes on the owner.

hints: The cat is the owner → cat + 's.

reteach.say: The long way says 'the tail of the cat'. Flip it: owner first — the cat — give the owner 's — the cat's — then the thing: the cat's tail. Same meaning, tidier label.

practiceBank.skill: flip 'the X of the Y' into 'the Y's X'

block.text: the lead of the dog → the ___ lead

wrongAnswers.why: missing apostrophe turns the owner into a plural
wrongAnswers.remedy: dogs with no apostrophe means many dogs. One dog OWNS this lead — mark the belonging.

wrongAnswers.why: 's drifted onto the thing
wrongAnswers.remedy: Ask the owner question out loud: who does the lead belong to? THAT word gets the 's.

hints: Say it the long way: the lead belongs to…?

reteach.say: Every flip is the same three steps: find the owner (the dog), give the owner 's (the dog's), then say what they own (the dog's lead). Let's do it slowly together.

practiceBank.skill: match long forms to belonging labels

block.prompt: Match each long phrase to its belonging label.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: the tail of the cat→the cat's tail, the bag of Sam→Sam's bag, the lead of the dog→the dog's lead, the desk of the tutor→the tutor's desk

wrongAnswers.answer: the bag of Sam → the dog's lead (mismatched pair)
wrongAnswers.why: matched by guessing instead of finding the owner
wrongAnswers.remedy: For each long phrase, ask 'who owns it?' first — then hunt for the label starting with that owner.

wrongAnswers.answer: reading cat's as 'more than one cat'
wrongAnswers.why: plural/possessive mix-up surfacing early
wrongAnswers.remedy: The apostrophe-s here means BELONGING, not lots. One cat, one tail, one owner.

hints: Find the owner in the long phrase — the label starts with them.
the desk of the tutor: the owner is the tutor.

reteach.say: Both sides say the same thing — one the long way, one as a label. The owner is your matching key: spot the owner in the long phrase, find the label that starts with that owner's name plus 's.

block.prompt: The coat belongs to the boy. Which is right?
block.explain: The boy is the owner, so boy gets 's: the boy's coat.

wrongAnswers.why: no apostrophe — belonging unmarked
wrongAnswers.remedy: One boy owns this coat. How do we mark an owner? Add the apostrophe-s to his name.

wrongAnswers.why: 's on the coat, not the boy
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does the coat own the boy? No! Who's the owner — and where must the 's sit?

hints: Owner question first: who owns the coat?

reteach.say: One more time, the owner rule: the OWNER gets the 's. The boy owns the coat, so we write the boy's coat. Try whispering 'who owns it?' before every answer — it never fails.

block.caption: the boy's coat — 's on the owner

practiceBank.skill: make belonging labels for real things

block.prompt: Make a belonging label for something real in your home — like Mum's mug or Rex's bowl.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: A real owner + 's + thing (e.g. Mum's mug), apostrophe before the s

wrongAnswers.why: apostrophe dropped in own writing
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read your label back: does the mug belong to Mum? Then Mum needs her belonging mark — where does it go?

wrongAnswers.why: owner and thing swapped
wrongAnswers.remedy: Labels start with the OWNER. Who owns it? Start with their name, add 's, then the thing.

hints: Pick the owner first, then what they own.

reteach.say: Let's build one together: think of someone in your family and one thing that's theirs. Owner's name… add 's… add the thing. That's a real belonging label you could stick on it!

block.prompt: Which sentence uses 's for BELONGING (not squashing)?
block.explain: Ben's kite = the kite belonging to Ben. The others are squashes: it's = it is, she's = she is, he's = he is.

wrongAnswers.why: took any apostrophe-s as belonging
wrongAnswers.remedy: Try the stretch test: it's raining → 'it is raining' — it fits! So that's a squash, Job 1. Which one can't be stretched to '… is'?

wrongAnswers.why: same slip — she's is squashed 'she is'
wrongAnswers.remedy: Stretch it: 'she is my best friend' — fits, so it's a squash. Find the one where 's means someone OWNS something.

hints: Try saying '… is' in place of each 's — if it fits, it's a squash.
Who actually OWNS something in one of these?

reteach.say: Same little mark, two jobs! Test any 's by stretching: if you can say 'is' — it's raining = it is raining — that's Job 1, squashing. If someone owns something — Ben's kite — that's Job 2, belonging. Detective test first, answer second.

block.prompt: Write a whole sentence with a belonging 's — and say who the owner is.
block.sample: I borrowed Mia's rubber. Mia is the owner.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: A sentence with owner + 's used correctly, owner named

wrongAnswers.answer: a sentence with the 's missing (Mias rubber)
wrongAnswers.why: the mark drops out under the load of writing a full sentence
wrongAnswers.remedy: Finish your sentence, then go back on owner patrol: does anything belong to anyone? Give the owner their 's.

wrongAnswers.answer: a plural mistaken for belonging (I have two cat's)
wrongAnswers.why: creeping greengrocer's apostrophe
wrongAnswers.remedy: Do the cats own anything in your sentence? If it just means MORE THAN ONE, no apostrophe — we'll hunt these properly next lesson!

hints: Say the sentence aloud before writing it.
Owner check at the end: who owns what, and did they get their 's?

reteach.say: Writers do an owner patrol after writing: read the sentence back and ask, does anything belong to anyone? If yes, the owner needs 's. Let's write one short sentence about something a friend or pet owns.

block.caption: write it → owner patrol → 's on the owner

practiceBank.skill: explain what a possessive phrase means

block.explain: The 's on Kim shows belonging: Kim's coat = the coat that belongs to Kim.

wrongAnswers.why: read the s as a plural s
wrongAnswers.remedy: There's an apostrophe before that s — that's the belonging mark, not a counting s. Who owns the coat?

wrongAnswers.why: read 's as squashed 'is' in the wrong spot
wrongAnswers.remedy: Try stretching: 'Kim is coat' — nonsense! So it's not a squash. What's the apostrophe's OTHER job?

hints: The 's sits on Kim — what does that tell you about Kim?
Say it the long way: the coat of…?

reteach.say: Reading a belonging label backwards: Kim's coat. The 's on Kim says Kim is the OWNER — so it means the coat belonging to Kim. Whenever you see name-apostrophe-s, think 'owner!'

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, interleave belonging with the Job 1 vs Job 2 stretch test.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach with the three-step flip (owner → owner+'s → thing), then a level-1 item.
adaptivity.masterySignal: 3+ correct across levels 2–3 including one flip of 'the X of the Y' and one own-written label → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'apostrophes for possession'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'let's find the owner first.'
Step down: underline the owner in the phrase; child only adds 's.
ONE hint: 'ask: who does it belong to?'
Keep it safe: 'Belonging is all about the owner — let's find who owns it.'
adaptivity.personalization: Build labels from the learner's real world — family names, pets, favourite toys (Mum's mug, Rex's bowl). The owner-question habit stays in every framing.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable label; praise the process — 'you found the owner every time and gave them their 's.'

differentiation.support: Phrase given with the owner underlined; child only adds 's. Stay on single clear owners (Sam, the cat).
differentiation.stretch: Rewrite 'the lead of the dog' and 'the desk of the tutor', then write a full sentence using a possessive 's ('I borrowed Mia's rubber.').

extension: Make belonging labels for three more real objects at home and read each aloud.
assessmentEvidence: Child writes at least three possessive phrases with 's correctly on the owner (e.g. Sam's bag, the dog's bone).
revisitLater: Lesson 13 — the apostrophe TRAP: NOT for plurals. Recall both jobs (squashing & belonging) as the only two times we DO use an apostrophe.
